brand.name: The AI Rishi
brand.description: A technology learning platform. The current program is FORGE-120: 120 days from system fundamentals to cloud, Kubernetes, reliability, retrieval, and controlled tool use. Content is free.

copy.heroDescription: FORGE-120 is a 120-day hands-on path from fundamentals through cloud, Kubernetes, AKS, and reliability, then retrieval and controlled tool use. The model is not the starting point.

story.whatBody: The AI Rishi is a technology learning and teaching platform. The current program is FORGE-120, a 120-day path from system fundamentals to retrieval and controlled tool use.
story.whyBody: A model can draft the files. Days 97–105 are where retrieval, policy, evaluation, and a disable path are taught. Until then, you still have to understand what ran.
story.methodBody: This is not a watch-and-copy course. Read the day, try it yourself, break one thing safely, debug what you see, then practise the questions. I will share exercises and interview questions. You still have to do the work.

methodSteps.title: Read
methodSteps.body: Understand the words. Predict what should happen before you run anything.

methodSteps.title: Try
methodSteps.body: Do the core task. On write days, your first version is yours — not AI's.

methodSteps.title: Break
methodSteps.body: Break one thing safely. Write down what you actually saw.

methodSteps.title: Debug
methodSteps.body: Logs, exit codes, and evidence. Chat is not a substitute for looking.

methodSteps.title: Practise
methodSteps.body: Answer the questions out loud. What fails, and how do you troubleshoot it?

methodSteps.title: Review
methodSteps.body: Check whether you can explain it. If you cannot, you do not own it yet.

story.pathBody: Deepen only when a real requirement demands it. CUDA, model training, multiple agent SDKs, and multiple vector databases stay outside the 120-day core.
story.communityTitle: If you want to learn with me
story.communityBody: If you are willing to put in the hours, you can learn along with me. I may help with doubts and debugging when the question shows real work.

about.title: Why I built this
about.intro: I wanted to get better at engineering. Not by hopping between tools, but by following one structured path until I could debug, review, and explain the work. Teaching what I understand is how I check whether I actually understood it.

sections.title: Why I started
sections.body: I did not want another pile of bookmarks. I wanted a path I could finish: understand the tool, use it, break it, and be able to talk about what failed. Writing it down is part of that. If I cannot explain something clearly, I still need to learn it.

sections.title: Why this order
sections.body: FORGE-120 is one path: foundations, then cloud, Kubernetes, reliability, retrieval, and controlled tool use. AI is not day 1. Day 59 is a read-only helper. Days 97–105 are the control layer. Day 105 is awareness, not an ML-infrastructure claim.

sections.title: How I want to learn and teach
sections.body: I am learning these technologies too, and I want to share what I understand along the way. I will try to help with doubts and debugging when the question shows real work. This is not a daily video course. I want people who will practise, analyse, and grow on their own — not people looking for a shortcut.

sections.title: What I will share
sections.body: Practical explanations. Exercises. Debugging situations. Practice questions. Interview questions. Things I think are worth understanding. Daily material, added as it is ready. You still have to do your own analysis.

sections.title: What you can expect
sections.body: A clear 120-day path, FORGE-120. Honesty about which days are published and which are still titles on the map. The work is still yours.

sections.title: What this is not
sections.body: Not a certificate mill, and not a job guarantee. Later, if the material is genuinely strong, I may offer paid group training. That is not this site today.

sections.title: Where the platform is going
sections.body: After day 120, deepen only what a real requirement demands: evaluation, observability, inference, or multi-cluster work. Those are not empty courses on this homepage.
